source_document.body:
2026 Paris Motor Show • Hyundai Tucson N Line Steals the Spotlight in Paris, but It's All Show and No Go
Honda Canceled Its Entire EV Lineup, but the Alpha Survived and It's Coming Soon
7 photos
Photo: Honda
Honda has officially confirmed that the production version of the 0 Alpha electric SUV will make its debut later this year. The news drops seven months after the Japanese automaker canceled almost its entire electric lineup and completely exited the North American EV market.
Honda scrapped its EV strategy in North America and made the news public in a press release on March 12, 2026. The decision was driven by a major reassessment of its global electrification strategy, due to the EV market meltdown, shifting government subsidy policies, and aggressive competition from Chinese automakers.
Honda was simply unable to deal with all these and canceled the launch of its highly promoted, upcoming in-house-developed electric vehicles that were only months away from going into production at Honda’s Marysville, Ohio, EV hub, retooled based on a massive investment to produce zero-tailpipe-emission cars.
That meant that the Honda 0 SUV , the Honda 0 Saloon, and the Acura RSX EV went straight to the cars' Valhalla without even seeing the light of day in production form. The sudden move led to an estimated $15.7 billion write-off. This adjustment forced Honda to report a net loss for the fiscal year ending March 2026, marking the company’s first annual consolidated operating loss in nearly 70 years.
Photo: Honda Just a few months later, in July 2026, Honda came up with one more cancellation. The automaker announced the complete discontinuation of the Honda Prologue, its only high-volume electric vehicle on sale in North America, by the end of the 2026 model year.
The Prologue sits on General Motors' BEV3 platform, sporting the Ultium battery architecture and sharing its chassis, powertrain, and electronics with the Chevrolet Blazer. The Prologue (still) rolls off the production line of the Ramos Arizpe factory in Mexico, which makes it a victim of the 25% tariffs on imported goods.
The production lines will stop in December 2026. Remaining dealership inventory is expected to completely sell out by the end of the first quarter of 2027. With this move, Honda is exiting the U.S. EV market , as the company fully redirected its resources into manufacturing gas-powered electric hybrids.
However, it turns out that the Japanese automaker still has something to say in the battery-electric car segment and officially confirmed the arrival of the Honda 0 Alpha SUV . Its global debut is set to take place on December 2, 2026, with deliveries starting in early 2027.
Photo: Honda For the moment, prototypes are undergoing road tests in India and Japan. Unofficial reports indicate that the production model will drop the "0 Alpha" designation and receive a new commercial name, set to be revealed shortly.
The model will retain the boxy design with the upright front fascia, supporting the illuminated redesigned "H" logo , a tall roofline, squared-off wheel arches, and flush door handles. A large central touchscreen, a digital instrument cluster, a panoramic roof, and Level 2 ADAS safety systems are expected to make their way on board the Honda 0 Alpha.
Built on Honda's first homegrown, in-house electric skateboard platform developed entirely from scratch, the 0 Alpha, or whatever its name will be, will be available with either the 61-kWh or the 75 kWh battery pack options.
The automaker is targeting a range of up to 404 miles (650 kilometers). However, that sounds overly optimistic. It will more likely be around 280 to 311 miles (450 to 500 kilometers) for the variant with the largest battery pack, in real driving conditions.
Photo: Honda The model will roll off the production line of Honda's Tapakura plant in Rajasthan, India, serving both domestic sales and international exports, including Japan, Thailand, Malaysia, Indonesia, and the Philippines.
Instead of targeting Western regions, Honda is shifting its EV focus, making the 0 Alpha off-limits for U.S. buyers. Why is that happening? It is obviously cheaper to engineer a car to meet the Asian market regulations than to develop it for the American or European markets, where stricter regulations would require a larger investment.
In the meantime, following the multi-billion-dollar EV write-off , Honda is reallocating its North American resources to an aggressive hybrid offensive of next-generation models. Honda is planning to introduce 15 new hybrid models globally by 2030, heavily focusing on North America.
The Ohio EV hub that was originally retrofitted to build the 0 Series EV s will be involved in other projects. Honda is investing $2 billion in an all-new manufacturing facility where it is planning to build a full-size three-row hybrid SUV. This marks Honda's first completely new assembly plant in North America in nearly two decades.
Photo: Honda The firm is still considering introducing EVs in America, but it is stepping back to reconsider its strategy. Seeing how automakers such as Ford, Slate, Hyundai and Kia, and Chevrolet offer affordable zero-tailpipe-emission models, Honda might as well consider joining the segment with a model to start under $30,000.
